$comment: EXP-1291 Threads v2: Team settings → Agents ×4, managed exactly like boards. The list = Settings rows (icon + color + name like a board row, then `New agent`); an agent page = the board page layout, `fields` top to bottom: identity (the board form's ONE field: icon picker + color swatch + name), Device (required; the device picker, online devices of the team the caller may start on), Account (the device's account picker, optional = the device's last used login; EXP-1306: the row's VALUE reads exactly like the composer's account picker chip = the picked login's agent brand mark + its email (`options` = the logins the device reports, `accountName` ladder; the agent-named stand-in row a profile-less device gets in the composer never counts), never the agent's name alone and never dimmed while editable; `agentAccountValue({options, account, cli})` replays `accountValueCases`: the option whose id == the pinned `account` (and whose agent == `cli` when set), else `cli`'s first option, else the last used option (isLastUsed), else the first; none = null and the row reads `copy.accountLastUsed` muted), Triggers (NEW-2: one row per trigger reading `triggerSummary`, a toggle per row, `+ Add` opens the trigger editor: a schedule = THE schedule picker (`schedule-picker.json`: Repeat · Days/Day · Time · Time zone rows; the stored form is a 5-field cron in an IANA zone, #N-2, never typed), an event = the name of an `events` row (the builtins `contract.events.builtinNames` or any custom name); none = the agent only waits for messages), Instructions (markdown, server-only: `sessions.getAgent`, placeholder `copy.instructionsPlaceholder`), Delete (owner-only, confirms with `copy.deleteConfirm`). Owner-only controls are hidden from members (they read). Save = `agents.create` for a new agent, `agents.update` after (NEW-2: an agent is a definition row; its conversations follow it). triggerSummary(trigger) (TS reference packages/domain-contract/src/agent-settings.ts; mirrors desktop domain::agent_settings, iOS AgentSettings.swift, Android AgentSettings.kt) replays `summaryCases`: schedule = `scheduleSummary(cron, tz)` of `schedule-picker.json` (`Every day at 09:00 (Europe/Vienna)`; a cron the rows cannot express reads `Cron …`); event = `copy.events[name]` for a builtin name, else `copy.event` with {name}; a disabled trigger appends ' · Paused'. validateAgentForm(form) replays `validationCases`: errors keyed by field, in field order: name blank (after trim) → copy.errors.nameRequired, over agentNameMax (contract sessionsSend) → copy.errors.nameTooLong, no device → copy.errors.deviceRequired, instructions over agentInstructionsMaxBytes UTF-8 bytes → copy.errors.instructionsTooLong; [] = valid.

actor.$comment: #EXP-1383: AGENTS ACT AS THEMSELVES. A write made by an agent session (any session of an AGENT TREE: its root has `agent_id`, or `started_by_agent_id` = a root an agent session started; the tree runs on a team-scoped key and its MCP access is clamped to the team; the server resolves it from the session the request speaks for, X-Exp-Session-Id or the agent credential, never from input) stamps the agent: `issue_events.actor_agent_id`, `comments.author_agent_id`, `issues.creator_agent_id` (FK agents, SET NULL; synced). The member column (`actor_user_id` / `author_id` / `creator_id`) keeps the member whose conversation it is, for audit. `issueActor({actorAgentId, actorUserId}, agents)` (TS reference src/agent-settings.ts; mirrors desktop domain::agent_settings, iOS AgentSettings.swift, Android AgentSettings.kt) replays `actorCases`: an agent id that resolves to a synced agent row = {kind: agent, id, name, icon, color}; else the user id = {kind: user, id}; else null (the server / a widget reporter). An agent actor renders EVERYWHERE a person would (timeline event rows, comment cards, the issue's Created-by row, notifications): its NAME where the person's name goes (`Sloppy changed status to Done`, the same per-type copy) and as the avatar the AGENT MARK = the agent's icon glyph in its color on the muted disc, the exact mark of the Chats agent bubbles and the Settings → Agents rows, at the avatar's size; never a person's initials and never the member's avatar. Activity folding keys the actor on the agent when set (activity-fold.json: an agent and its member are DIFFERENT actors; two agents of one member are different actors). Notifications name the agent (`Sloppy commented on EXP-12`).

assignee.$comment: #EXP-1383: ASSIGN ISSUES TO AGENTS. `issues.assignee_agent_id` (+ `issue_drafts.assignee_agent_id`; FK agents, SET NULL; synced) is MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE with `assignee_id` (DB check: at most one set); setting one clears the other in the same write. THE assignee picker ×4 (styleguide `picker-assignee`, no new component) lists `copy.unassigned`, the team's members, then the team's agents straight after the members, no heading (S-3: never another member's Assistant (`visibleAgent`); the server refuses one as an assignee, an existing assignment to it still reads like any agent's; sorted by sortOrder then name; each row = the agent mark + name; `assigneeOptions` replays `optionCases`, ids `user:<id>` / `agent:<id>`), search matches agent names too. The selected agent reads like a member everywhere an assignee shows (issue rows, the detail property row, the board card): the agent mark + name. A solo team hides its assignee control only while it has no agents (an agent is someone to assign to). `My issues` stays the viewer's OWN `assignee_id`. The `assignee_changed` event payload keeps `from`/`to` (user ids) and adds `fromAgentId`/`toAgentId`; the timeline reads the agent's name (`assigned Sloppy`). On ANY new assignee (any path: tRPC, MCP `issues update {assigneeAgentId}`, a draft create; never the solo-team default on create) the server, in the same transaction, emits the builtin team event `issue.assigned` {issueId, identifier, title, assigneeId, assigneeAgentId}; on an assignment TO an agent it also posts a NUDGE card into the ASSIGNER's conversation with that agent (created if missing; THE event trigger's firing: a `trigger_fired` card {name: `issue.assigned`, eventId, issueId, triggerId: null} drawing the conversation's usual `Trigger fired: {name}` line (session-thread.json), `copy.nudge` = the message body the agent reads) and relays it so a live engine wakes; an agent assigning itself never nudges itself, and an assigner who is an agent session nudges as its member.

assistant.$comment: S-3 (owner 2026-10-28): THE ASSISTANT ×4. Every member has ONE Assistant per team (`agents.role = assistant`, contract `agentRole`; unique (team_id, owner_id) where role = assistant), the orchestrator they talk to and the one with the voice. It is created ON FIRST USE (`agents.ensureAssistant {teamId}`: the composer home, the Settings Agents group and the chat list call it; it runs on the member's own newest desktop, else their newest device, else it is not created yet and the page reads `copy.noDevice`); the migration made each member's voice agent (user_voice_settings.agentId, when they own it) their Assistant. OWNED by its member: only they see it in the Settings Agents group, the composer's agent row, the chats list and the assignee picker (`visibleAgent`: another member's Assistant is never listed), only they edit it, nobody deletes it (a team owner's `agents.delete` is refused too). AVATAR = the Exponential brand mark in the foreground colour on bg muted, never a stored icon or colour (icon/color stay null). NAME = `copy.name` unless the member renames it. TRIGGERS = exactly one schedule PRESET (`schedules`, picker rows, the `Check in` section; `off` = no trigger) and never an event (`agents.update` refuses anything else: `assistantScheduleOf` must not return null for the stored triggers); team agents keep the trigger list + prompt. #EXP-1439: its PROMPT is built in (`prompt`, versioned: `version` bumps re-stamp every Assistant's `instructions_updated_at`, so a live conversation shows the existing Instructions changed hint and relaunches on the new text); `agents.instructions` is never read for an Assistant and `agents.update` refuses it (`copy.promptFixed`). The migration that removed the field posted each member's old text ONCE into their Assistant conversation (`copy.legacyInstructions`, a system row). THE PAGE (`sections` top to bottom, the agent page's layout and controls): identity (name only, the brand mark instead of the icon picker), `runs-on` (THE device / account / model pickers, the agent page's rows; the MODEL row's value = `assistantModelValue({model, cli})` (`modelValueCases`): the pinned `model` when set (non-blank), else the dispatcher root's default for the login's CLI (contract deviceAgentDefaults `threadModel`, `codexThreadModel` for codex; no CLI = claude), the model its conversation actually runs — never `Last used`, never empty, identical ×4; the Assistant's device IS the member's voice device; the server mirrors it into user_voice_settings.voiceDeviceId/agentId for old clients and the voice runtime), `check-in` (THE Picker over `schedules`), `voice` (the voice.json Settings group MOVED as one block, its rows unchanged minus `copy.voiceDevice` and `copy.agent`: the device is Runs on's, the agent is this Assistant; the meeting rows follow). No instructions section, no Delete. A SHARED device (lifecycle SLOP-2): the Assistant runs on the member's OWN login there (`account` = theirs); meeting mode keeps its privacy gate (meeting-access.ts).

copy.legacyInstructions: Your Assistant now runs on Exponential's built-in prompt, so its instructions field is gone. Your old instructions, to move into a team agent if you still need them:

prompt.text:
You are this member's Assistant in this team: the main agent that manages every other chat, agent and pull request they have here. They talk to you; you run the rest.

Your job: know at all times what each of their chats and agents is doing (progressing, stuck, waiting on them, done). Start, steer, nudge, move and end their chats to get the work done. Answer a chat's question yourself when what they told you settles it; escalate only real decisions.

Your status card: keep ONE live status card (an Exponential UI surface via exponential_show): in progress (chat, PR, state), shipped since they last wrote, stuck, decisions needed. Every surface you show updates that card in place. Keep it short: one row per chat, newest first; drop finished items once they have seen them.

When to speak: write a message only (a) to answer the member after they write, or (b) when a decision needs them: then use exponential_show ask with clear options (it notifies them). Scheduled check-ins, a PR opened, still running, a child's routine reply: update the card and end your turn silently. Never repeat what the card already says.

Scope: only this team exists for you: its boards, people, devices and sessions. Never use a device or account of another team.

Style: short, concrete, no filler. Name issues as #IDENT.

chat.$comment: #EXP-1439 (owner 2026-10-30): THE ASSISTANT'S CHAT STAYS QUIET, server-enforced (lib/agents/assistant-chat.ts), so every client renders it with the existing rows and cards unchanged. (1) STATUS CARD: in its root conversation every `exponential_show` SURFACE edits the newest surface card the conversation posted since the member last wrote (their message, or their answer to its question/plan); none = a new card. So between two member messages there is ONE status card, updated in place across turns. (2) TEXT only in a turn the member started (among the inputs delivered last, one is theirs): a turn woken by a check-in tick or a child's line posts no text (dropped, the reply is a no-op). (3) A DECISION is an ask (question/plan): a new card plus ONE push to its owner (`agent_message`, title `copy.decisionPush`, body = the question or the plan's first line). (4) SILENT EVENTS: the bus lines in `silentEvents` never land in an Assistant conversation (its next check-in reads them); asks, walls, stuck/unclaimed and reports still do. (5) QUIET TICKS: a scheduled check-in is skipped when none of the member's sessions in the team (their threads, their agents' conversations, every child; not the Assistant's own conversation) moved since its last firing.
